About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page

About the team

Mexico FP&A is the finance partner of the Mexico business. We sit between the product, credit, growth and marketing teams and the country leadership, and our job is to make sure every bet the business makes is sized, challenged and reflected in the P&L before it is made.

We are not a reporting team. We work hand in hand with Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta (deposits and transactional) and Growth stakeholders, as well as Treasury, Controllership, Public Policy, Second Line Risk and Investor Relations, to turn strategy into numbers and numbers into decisions.

How we work

  • We are owners: we make things happen instead of waiting for them.

  • We have a bias to output: fast, right-sized answers over months-long projects.

  • We set the finance agenda, not only serve it.

  • We embrace conflicting ideas and question the status quo, with data.

  • We work hard, with integrity and putting the team first.

About the role

As the IC7 in Mexico FP&A for credit products and strategic planning, you are the senior analytical bridge between Mexico's credit products, the P&L and the planning process. You do not run closings or own the budget calendar. You own something harder: making sure what goes into the plan is grounded, challenged and financially sound, and that leadership decides with the right numbers in front of them.

The role has three faces. You are a business partner to Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core, who challenges their strategy and helps them bake initiatives into the plan. You are a first responder who quantifies, within days, anything that hits the P&L that wasn't planned. And you are a decision shaper who builds the frameworks, tools and governance leadership uses to decide.

At this level you set the finance agenda rather than wait for requests. You work directly with the country CEO, CFO and business-unit leaders, move between hands-on modeling and executive framing in the same week, and raise the analytical bar of the team around you.

What you will do

1. Partner with product teams and bake their initiatives into the plan

  • Understand the projections of Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core teams and challenge the strategy behind them: assumptions, timing, certainty and whether the impact is really incremental.

  • Help teams translate initiatives into P&L impact when they don't know how, and carry them into budget, rebudget, forecast checkpoints and the 5-year plan.

  • Size initiatives with a consistent toolkit (NPV, CAC, payback, ROAS, gross profit) and apply clear inclusion criteria.

  • Push back when a plan doesn't add up and perform deep dives proactively, for example recommending not to launch a program until its economics are positive, and proposing alternatives such as phased rollouts or test budgets.

2. React fast to anything that hits the P&L unplanned

  • Be the first to quantify regulatory and market shocks.

  • Turn the impact into options: mitigation levers, owners and dates, not only a number.

  • Detect and escalate data and accounting anomalies that distort the P&L.

3. Be the analytical bridge between credit products, the P&L and planning

  • Challenge investments and strengthen how decisions are made with clear argumentation.

  • Build tools leadership can use directly that help in the decision-making process.

  • Propose and drive decision governance, especially on when Finance must be involved.

4. Communicate to executives and raise the bar of the team

  • Prepare materials for executives with a clear narrative, grounded in numbers.

  • Support regulatory deliverables.

  • Coach analysts on the team and set the bar for analytical rigor.

What we are looking for

Must have

  • Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Actuarial Science or a related quantitative field; a master's degree is a plus.

  • 8+ years of experience in FP&A, business analytics, strategy or credit analytics, with a significant part in consumer credit, banking or fintech.

  • Track record of changing senior leadership decisions with analysis: stopping, reshaping or accelerating initiatives based on their economics.

  • Deep unit-economics and credit knowledge: NPV, CAC and payback, ROAS and incrementality, cost of risk, provisions (IFRS 9), funds transfer pricing, interchange, and how credit policy flows into the P&L.

  • Hands-on analytical skills: SQL, financial modeling and spreadsheets; Python or notebooks is a strong plus. You build your own data instead of waiting for it.

  • Ability to lead cross-functional analyses end to end with Product, Credit, Treasury, Controllership, Risk and Public Policy, and to influence without authority.

  • Executive communication: turn complex analysis into a one-page story and a clear recommendation for C-level audiences.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you can size an unplanned impact in days and refine it later.

  • Experience coaching or mentoring analysts.

  • Fluency in Spanish and English.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Mexican financial regulation or regulated banking entities.

  • Experience with planning tools such as Anaplan.

  • Experience designing experiments or incrementality tests.

  • Fluency with AI tools to speed up analysis and build lightweight dashboards and calculators

 

Work Setup

Location

Mexico City

Work model

[Hybrid / On-Site]

Office requirement

2 days per week at the office.

 

Our Benefits

MEXICO JOBS:

  • Chance of earning equity at Nubank

  • Food Card

  • NuCare – Psychological, Financial and Legal Assistance Program

  • Life Insurance

  • Medical Plan

  • Dental Plan

  • NuLanguage – Language Course Program

  • Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

  • Extended Parental Leave

  • Daycare Allowance

  • Parental Consultancy

  • Work-from-home Allowance

  • Gym Partnerships

  • Holiday Bonus ("Aguinaldo") of 30 days of pay per year

  • 17 days of paid vacation with 25% vacation bonus

  • Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable

About the Role

Nubank’s Talent Acquisition team is the architectural backbone of our culture. As we continue to scale and innovate, the people we hire in the next 12–24 months will shape the company’s trajectory across one of our most strategic and competitive talent markets.

As a Recruiter Expert, you will own high-impact hiring across key business and functional areas. You’ll serve as a strategic recruiting partner for senior leadership, leveraging Nubank’s strong market presence while finding creative ways to attract, engage, and close top-tier passive talent in a highly competitive landscape.


You’ll be Responsible for

  • Owning full-cycle recruiting for strategic, senior, and specialized roles across the organization

  • Building deep passive candidate pipelines using advanced sourcing intelligence — going beyond traditional channels to find top talent where they actually engage, through niche communities, referrals, and industry networks

  • Acting as a strategic talent advisor to senior leadership: shaping role profiles, defining hiring bars, and translating business goals into actionable hiring strategies

  • Using data to manage pipeline health proactively — building dashboards, tracking funnel conversion, and communicating insights clearly with senior stakeholders

  • Designing and iterating on scalable hiring processes that ensure an exceptional candidate experience

  • Strengthening and evolving Nubank’s employer brand to stand out and attract top-tier talent in Brazil

 

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

  • A proven track record of full-cycle recruiting, with demonstrated depth in engaging and closing passive candidates for senior, leadership, or specialized roles

  • Hands-on sourcing expertise for hard-to-fill positions, bringing creative tactics and diverse talent channels to the table

  • Strong business acumen and functional fluency, with the ability to quickly understand new domains, calibrate talent independently, and adapt to different business needs

  • A data-driven approach to pipeline management: someone who builds their own reporting, uses metrics to influence strategy, and knows when to escalate and when to pivot

  • The ability to operate with high autonomy in ambiguous, fast-paced environments — building structure, managing multiple competing priorities, and maintaining a high quality bar

  • Experience partnering with senior leadership as a true, consultative talent advisor

  • Fluency in English and Portuguese

About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page

About the team

Mexico FP&A is the finance partner of the Mexico business. We sit between the product, credit, growth and marketing teams and the country leadership, and our job is to make sure every bet the business makes is sized, challenged and reflected in the P&L before it is made.

We are not a reporting team. We work hand in hand with Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta (deposits and transactional) and Growth stakeholders, as well as Treasury, Controllership, Public Policy, Second Line Risk and Investor Relations, to turn strategy into numbers and numbers into decisions.

How we work

  • We are owners: we make things happen instead of waiting for them.

  • We have a bias to output: fast, right-sized answers over months-long projects.

  • We set the finance agenda, not only serve it.

  • We embrace conflicting ideas and question the status quo, with data.

  • We work hard, with integrity and putting the team first.

About the role

As a Mexico FP&A Senior Specialist, you sit at the intersection of Nu México’s financial execution, regulatory discipline, and forward planning. You serve as the operational anchor for Mexico’s consolidated figures, ensuring that key consolidated financial outputs reported to management, the Board of Directors, and regulators are reliable, structurally sound, and delivered on time. In this role, you lead the monthly close, consolidate financial statements and KPIs, and turn variance analysis into clear executive materials for local leadership, Holdings, Investor Relations, and regulatory authorities.

Beyond recurring cycles, you act as an analytical first responder for complex, ad-hoc analyses. This demands both advanced corporate finance expertise and close cross-functional coordination to clarify technical details, align business assumptions, and secure the agreements needed to deliver rigorous analysis. At this level, you bridge technical modeling with executive decision-making, ensuring leadership moves forward with numbers that are both rigorous and grounded.


What you will do

1. Deliver recurring financial operations

  • Coordinate and execute Mexico’s monthly close, driving end-to-end planning and alignment across local and global finance teams.

  • Consolidate financial statements and core KPIs, preparing executive management materials and partnering across business units to explain variances and deliver deep-dive analyses.

  • Deliver specialized financial reporting for executive stakeholders, including the Board of Directors, Investor Relations (IR), and mandatory or ad-hoc regulatory requirements (e.g., CNBV).

2. Drive planning and forecasting cycles

  • Consolidate Mexico’s budget and forecast figures, including financial statements, KPIs, assumptions, and business narrative, leveraging advanced corporate finance and financial modeling expertise.

  • Partner with Business Units (BUs) and efficiency business partners to challenge, validate, and accurately reflect assumptions in financial plans.

  • Build and align the budget narrative across cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders to ensure strategic consistency.

3. Lead structural projects and ad-hoc financial analysis

  • Conduct high-impact, ad-hoc financial analyses on complex, non-recurring issues (such as capital requirements, structural business changes, or regulatory shifts) to support strategic decision-making.

  • Manage initiatives to optimize and scale financial models, ensuring they reflect evolving business needs and maintain structural integrity.

  • Contribute to model and infrastructure roadmaps, translating business requirements into technical enhancements and tooling improvements (e.g., Anaplan).

What we are looking for

Must have

  • Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Actuarial Science or a related quantitative field.

  • 3-4 years of experience in FP&A, business analytics, strategy or credit analytics, with a significant part in consumer credit, banking or fintech.

  • Advanced financial modeling and forecasting skills.

  • Advanced skills across Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 ecosystems.

  • Knowledge of Mexican GAAP and IFRS accounting standards.

  • Ability to explain complex financial information clearly to senior stakeholders.

  • Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder alignment.

  • Strong prioritization skills and the ability to manage recurring deadlines alongside urgent requests.

  • Spanish and English fluency.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Mexican financial regulation or regulated banking entities.

  • Experience with planning tools such as Anaplan.

  • Experience navigating, extracting, or validating financial data across Mexican financial regulatory portals and databases (e.g., CNBV, Banxico).

  • Fluency with AI tools to speed up analysis and build lightweight dashboards and calculators.

 

Work Setup

Location

Mexico City

Work model

[Hybrid / On-Site]

Office requirement

2 days per week at the office.

 

Our Benefits

MEXICO JOBS:

  • Chance of earning equity at Nubank

  • Food Card

  • NuCare – Psychological, Financial and Legal Assistance Program

  • Life Insurance

  • Medical Plan

  • Dental Plan

  • NuLanguage – Language Course Program

  • Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

  • Extended Parental Leave

  • Daycare Allowance

  • Parental Consultancy

  • Work-from-home Allowance

  • Gym Partnerships

  • Holiday Bonus ("Aguinaldo") of 30 days of pay per year

  • 17 days of paid vacation with 25% vacation bonus

  • Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable

About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page

About the Team

The Legal team partners with Nubank's leadership, Board and regulated entities across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and the United States. This role sits in a small, high-visibility team under the Chief Legal Officer that owns governance for the parent company and sets the standards that bank and other regulated-entity boards follow as well as advises on all public company reporting and issuer matters.

Day to day, you will work alongside the CLO, CFO and the executive team, and with Finance, Investor Relations, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, regional legal and regulatory teams, and outside counsel across several jurisdictions.

About the Role

As a public company, Nubank needs governance and reporting that work end to end: from the parent Board and its committees down to every regulated entity in the group. This role leads that model. You will serve as Assistant Corporate Secretary to the parent company and be a trusted partner to directors and executives, while owning the company's SEC and NYSE reporting program and the global standards for how subsidiary and bank boards operate.

You will also be the execution engine behind large, strategic corporate initiatives, turning legal requirements into clear ownership, milestones and decisions across many moving parts. This is a big remit with direct exposure to the Board and executive team.

You will:

  • Run Board and committee processes end to end, so directors receive well-prepared, decision-focused materials on time.

  • Lead SEC and NYSE reporting, with disciplined disclosure controls and timely, consistent filings.

  • Build the readiness plan, owners, controls and systems for the evolution of the company's public-company reporting and governance requirements.

  • Set a global governance baseline for regional bank and subsidiary boards, adapted to local law and supervisory expectations.

  • Drive cross-functional corporate, legal-entity and capital-markets projects from kickoff to close.

As a senior leadership role, this position is subject to Nu’s Global Statutory Officer Policy and involves appointment across applicable group entities. Final designation remains contingent upon local legal, compliance, and regulatory clearances.

Key Responsibilities and Expectations

Board and corporate secretary support

  • Coordinate with the CLO, annual Board and committee calendar, agendas, materials, minutes, resolutions and evaluations, and attend Board meetings.

  • Manage director onboarding, committee charters, governance policies and annual shareholder meetings.

  • Help the team adopt the operating rhythms of a public company board, and prepare executives to present to directors with confidence.

Public company reporting and securities compliance

  • Lead the SEC and NYSE reporting program under the current foreign private issuer framework, including Form 20-F, Form 6-K, registration statements and related disclosure processes.

  • Coordinate drafting, review, certifications, filing calendars and approvals with Finance, Investor Relations, Treasury, Risk, Compliance and business leaders.

  • Prepare the organization for expanded reporting and governance requirements, including disclosure controls, calendars, systems and cross-functional ownership.

  • Oversee, with Compliance, insider-reporting and securities-compliance processes, including Section 16 filings, trading windows, insider lists and related policies.

Global and regulated-entity governance

  • Define global baseline standards for subsidiary and bank boards: structure, reserved matters, delegated authority, escalation, minutes, materials and records.

  • Advise on governance requirements for regulated financial institutions in the United States and Latin America, working with local legal and regulatory teams on independence, notifications and supervisory matters.

  • Make sure the parent Board understands what is happening at the local level, and that local boards align with group expectations.

Corporate projects and legal-entity management

  • Lead or support financings, capital-markets transactions, M&A, reorganizations and large legal-entity structuring initiatives, project-managing counsel across jurisdictions.

  • Own global legal-entity governance and lifecycle management: formation, maintenance, annual filings, officer and director appointments, powers of attorney, signatory authorities, reorganizations and dissolutions.

Outside counsel, process and innovation

  • Manage outside counsel and specialist providers with clear scopes, budgets and accountability.

  • Improve templates, processes, technology and governance data as the company grows, and adopt AI and automation responsibly, with confidentiality safeguards and human review.

Qualifications

Professional Experience & Education

  • Law degree; admission to practice law in the United States (New York preferred). Brazilian qualification is a plus.

  • 10-15 years of relevant legal experience in corporate governance, securities, public-company reporting or corporate legal work, including meaningful responsibility for Board and committee matters.

  • Training at a leading U.S. law firm, advising public companies, or financial institutions.

  • In-house experience at a regulated financial institution, fintech or large regulated, international group (banking, payments, consumer finance, lending, broker-dealer or digital assets), advising across legal, regulatory, product and business teams.

  • Familiarity with banking regulation and regulated-entity governance in the United States and Latin America; depth in Brazil preferred, Mexico, Colombia or other regional markets valuable.

  • Working knowledge of SEC requirements for foreign private issuers and U.S. domestic registrants, NYSE listing standards and public-company disclosure controls.

  • Experience as a corporate secretary, assistant secretary or senior governance counsel supporting a public-company Board and committees, including drafting materials and minutes and advising directors and executives.

  • Experience coordinating multi-jurisdictional work with local and international counsel.

Competencies & Attributes

  • Ability to work comfortably with senior leaders and directors in both the United States and Brazil.

  • Has executive presence and can explain complex matters clearly and with poise.

  • Ability to influence senior leaders and directors in the U.S. and Brazil, and align stakeholders across time zones and functions.

  • Very detail-oriented and organized, able to manage many parallel workstreams, deadlines and moving parts without losing accuracy.

  • Ability to turn legal requirements into plain language for non-lawyers.

  • Ownership and urgency: delivers with limited supervision, follows through and removes obstacles.

Role Details

Location: Brazil or the United States. The role requires travel to São Paulo and to Board meetings in the US.

Reports To: This position reports to the Chief Legal Officer, who is based in the US.

About the role

  • At Nubank, hiring and moving talent across borders is a core part of how we grow. The Talent Acquisition team operates at high speed and scale, and the systems that support it need to match that pace. As a Senior IT Engineer in the Automations & Internal Systems pillar, you will design and build the internal systems and automations that power our recruiting operation.

  • This is a high-impact, AI-first engineering role. You will understand real operational problems, build solutions using the tools that fit best (from n8n and AI APIs to production-grade services), and progressively evolve the most critical solutions into robust systems on Nubank’s core engineering stack. You’ll work on projects ranging from recruiting workflows to cross-functional, business-critical systems, including regulated processes such as background checks.

You'll be responsible for

  • Internal Systems Development: Designing, building, and evolving internal systems that support Talent Acquisition and related operations, including new checks and integrations with external vendors for regulated processes.

  • From Automation to Production Services: Taking solutions originally built in low-code tools like Apps Script and rebuilding them as scalable, maintainable services on Nubank’s core engineering stack (Clojure, Datomic, AWS), as part of our migration toward canonical technologies.

  • Automation Development: Designing and building robust automations and cross-system integrations, using n8n as our main platform together with internal APIs and tools.

  • AI-First Engineering: Applying an AI-first mindset to everything you build, leveraging tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Glean to develop intelligent, agentic solutions that replace or augment manual processes.

  • Systems Integration: Designing and maintaining reliable data flows between recruiting systems and other internal platforms, ensuring data integrity and security.

  • Problem Discovery: Partnering with business stakeholders and recruiters to understand their challenges, prioritize opportunities, and define the right solution, with a focus on efficiency, accuracy, and user experience.

  • Collaboration: Working alongside other technical partners in the Talent Efficiency pillar, accountable for automations and internal systems, as well as recruiters and business partners, to deliver solutions aligned with real operational needs.

  • Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Maintaining clear documentation, including flow diagrams, technical docs, and user guides, to ensure maintainability and knowledge transfer.

  • Innovation: Staying current with emerging engineering and AI trends, and proactively evaluating new tools and methodologies.

We are looking for a person who has

  • Solid professional experience in software development, including building and maintaining backend services or internal systems.

  • Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language (such as Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, or Clojure).

  • Proven experience building with AI/LLM APIs, including prompt engineering, agentic workflows, and tools such as Claude, Gemini, or GPT.

  • Solid experience with RESTful API design and integrations with external web services.

  • Strong knowledge of development best practices: code versioning, testing, code review, and design patterns.

  • Ability to analyze, document, and optimize processes before building solutions for them.

  • Clear and effective communication skills, able to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders.

  • Advanced English proficiency.

Location for this opportunity (City, Country)

  • São Paulo, Brazil

Our Benefits

  • Chance of earning equity at Nubank

  • Food/ Meal Card (Vale-Refeição and/or Vale Alimentação)

About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page


About the Team

People Journey & Culture brings together Culture, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging, Learning & Development, and Purple Journey & Performance. Together, we help build high-performing teams, strengthen Nubank's culture and create connected, meaningful experiences that enable Nubankers to do the best work of their lives.

Within PJC, L&D drives continuous learning through strategies, products and experiences that strengthen individual and team performance and support business success. We combine thoughtful human experiences with scalable, personalized and AI-enabled solutions, choosing the approach that best fits each audience and need.

About the Role

We are looking for an L&D Senior Specialist to lead development initiatives for Nubank's Engineering teams. You will work closely with Engineering leaders and partners to understand their context, identify capability and performance needs, and turn business priorities into practical learning plans and programs.

This is a senior individual contributor role at the intersection of strategy and execution. You will own complex initiatives end to end, exercise judgment in ambiguous and changing situations, influence partners without relying on formal authority, and use evidence to improve outcomes. You will bring deep L&D expertise, creativity and an AI-first mindset to develop solutions that engage engineers and strengthen their ability to deliver business impact.


You’ll be Responsible for

  • Understand the business and diagnose needs: Build a close understanding of Engineering's strategy, operating context, audiences and challenges. Combine stakeholder input, data and observation to identify capability gaps, distinguish learning needs from other performance factors, and prioritize opportunities.

  • Translate strategy into action: Turn strategic priorities and identified needs into a clear, prioritized development plan, with defined audiences, outcomes, milestones, ownership and measures of success. Adapt the plan as the business context evolves.

  • Design and deliver development programs: Lead the design, development, implementation and improvement of learning experiences for Engineering teams. Apply adult learning and instructional design methods, selecting the right mix of formal, experiential, social and on-the-job learning for each challenge.

  • Own projects end to end: Manage scope, timelines, dependencies, resources, risks and decisions across concurrent initiatives. Coordinate internal experts, facilitators and external partners where appropriate, communicate progress and resolve obstacles to deliver quality outcomes.

  • Partner and influence: Build trusted relationships with Engineering leaders, technical subject matter experts, Centers of Excellence, People partners and other stakeholders. Align expectations, navigate competing priorities and influence decisions through clear recommendations and evidence.

  • Measure and improve impact: Define success measures and a practical evaluation approach from the start. Track reach, engagement, learning and application, as well as relevant performance or business outcomes where feasible. Interpret results and feedback, communicate insights and adjust solutions over time.

  • Create and scale with AI: Experiment with AI and digital tools to design, personalize and deliver learning solutions, improve the employee experience, increase engagement and expand impact. Choose intentionally between scalable self-service and high-touch experiences.

  • Bring expertise and fresh perspectives: Stay current on L&D practices, learning technologies and the evolving needs of technical teams. Share knowledge and contribute to improving how the L&D team works.


We're Looking For Someone Who Has

Required

  • Demonstrated experience developing technical teams, with the ability to understand their context and partner effectively with technical experts.

  • Strong project and program management experience, including leading complex initiatives from diagnosis and planning through delivery, measurement and iteration.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with experience building trust, influencing without formal authority and aligning people with different perspectives and priorities.

  • Ability to interpret business context, navigate ambiguity and changing scenarios, make sound decisions and translate strategic needs into actionable development plans.

  • Experience defining meaningful metrics, analyzing quantitative and qualitative evidence, following up on results and using insights to improve learning solutions.

  • Creativity and problem-solving skills, with a track record of designing practical solutions suited to the audience and the challenge.

  • Experience using AI and digital learning tools to develop or improve solutions, support engagement and extend reach or impact.

  • Fluent English.

  • Experience developing Engineering teams, including working closely with engineering leaders and technical subject matter experts.

  • Experience in a fast-paced technology environment.

São Paulo - Brazil

Hybrid

Office requirement

3 days per week at the office.

About the Role

The Compensation Expert will act as a bridge between global Total Rewards strategy and business execution. Serving as a trusted consultant to HRBPs and leadership, the role protects our compensation philosophy while leading essential employee lifecycle processes, including job architecture, salary offers, annual and mid-year cycles, off cycle retention, equity management, and data integrity.

We are seeking a strategic, highly analytical, and action oriented Compensation Expert for our Total Rewards team. Based within the Foundations & Intelligence division, you will serve as the technical lead for key compensation initiatives, such as benchmark salary range updates, global compensation cycles, market intelligence analysis, and advisory support for business leaders and HRBPs.


You’ll be Responsible for

  • Salary Range Management & Review: Lead the end to end analysis and update of global salary ranges (LATAM, US, Europe) based on market data (Towers, AON, Pave) and internal equity.

  • Compensation Cycles (Year End & Mid Year): Plan, structure and execute guidance for Year End and Mid Year merit, promotion and equity (RSU) cycles, ensuring alignment with budget and Pay for Performance philosophy.

  • Compensation Advisory: Serve as a technical advisor for HRBPs and directors/executives on proactive/reactive retention cases, exceptional hire packages, and internal moves.

  • Data Analysis & Market Intelligence: Build financial models and complex simulations for total people cost, RSU impact, retention and benefit equalization, and collective agreement impacts (CBA / BRA Data Base “Dissídio”).

  • Governance & Strategic Projects: Ensure regulatory compliance of compensation packages (e.g., rules for positions of trust / PoT, statutory directors / BACEN) and collaborate on improvements to internal compensation tools (MyComp, Visier, Oracle).

 

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

Required

  • Advanced Compensation Experience: Strong track record managing pay structures, long-term incentives (RSU/SOP), market intelligence, and global compensation cycles in tech or financial services.

  • Analytical Capability: Advanced proficiency in financial modeling and analytical tools (advanced Google Sheets; BigQuery or analytics platforms like Visier are a plus).

  • Business Acumen & Assertive Communication: Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders (M-Team / VPs), contextualize technical recommendations clearly, and run complex projects autonomously.

  • Project Management: Can participate in any Comp project regardless of business or area of expertise. Leads medium to large impact/scale/complexity projects and develops to lead larger initiatives. Ensures project stakeholder and communications management, and serves as the interface with Comp Champions (business inputs/outputs) and relevant areas of expertise. Relies on guidance from the Comp Leadership team as needed.

  • Languages: Advanced/Fluent English for daily interaction with international stakeholders and consumption of global market materials.

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

About the Team

The Credit Risk Squad is part of the 2nd line of defense, responsible for managing and overseeing the credit risk function of our organization by providing independent oversight and challenge to the first line of defense. Within it, the Provisions team creates the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models used to calculate loss allowances, participating end to end in model development, implementation, monitoring, data quality and support to Finance accounting teams. Our models feed Nubank's financial statements under IFRS 9 and local regulation, including CMN Resolution 4,966/2021 and BCB Resolution 352/2023 in Brazil.

About the Role

As a Retail Credit Risk Senior Specialist focused on Brazil, you'll be the focal point for everything related to Res. 4966 expected credit loss provisioning. You'll proactively identify and control gaps in the models and in the processes built around them, from inputs and model implementation to closing and regulatory reporting. That means making sure models comply with regulatory expectations, produce the correct data for accounting and regulatory reports, and that ECL movements are understood, controlled and well explained.

You'll also be a primary point of contact for the local regulator (BCB) and the external auditors (KPMG) on the local models, working alongside the team's leadership. This is an individual-contributor role with high visibility among senior stakeholders in Finance, Risk and the local CRO's office.


You’ll be Responsible for

  • Own the Res. 4966 ECL provisioning chain — be the team's focal point on the local models, monthly closing and the data they produce for accounting and regulatory reports.

  • Identify and close gaps proactively — assess models and surrounding processes (inputs, implementation, closing, reporting) against regulatory expectations, and drive the plan to close them.

  • Explain and control ECL movements — make sure monthly provision movements are understood, controlled and clearly explained to the Global Credit Director and the BR local CRO.

  • Resolve BACEN demands and make them repeatable — answer ad-hoc regulatory requests promptly, and build the answers into standing processes and monitoring so the same question is never investigated twice.

  • Be the face of the local models with BCB and KPMG — act as the named counterpart for regulator and auditor questions, and as backup to leadership in regulator meetings.

  • Automate and scale with AI — automate well-established local processes (e.g., the monthly Highlights deck, closing steps, pipeline validation) and build an internal Res. 4966 context library so other teams can self-serve 4966 knowledge and analysis.

 

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Statistics, Math, or a related quantitative field.

  • Hands-on experience with Brazilian provisioning regulation, specifically CMN Resolution 4,966/2021 and BCB Resolution 352/2023.

  • Strong communication skills in English, written and spoken.

  • Strong communication skills and a demonstrated ability to transfer technical knowledge to non-specialists and teammates.

  • Comfortable operating with high visibility across senior internal stakeholders (global credit leadership, Finance, local CRO's office).

Nice to Have

  • Experience interacting with regulators and external auditors on provisioning or expected-credit-loss matters.

  • Exposure to IFRS 9 or other international provisioning standards, and experience with model transitions between accounting frameworks.

  • Coding/technical skills sufficient to engage with model implementation (Python/SQL).

  • Experience mentoring or growing into people leadership.

About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page

About the Role

This role leads analytics for two scopes, Contestation and Fraud Security Features, and is accountable for the analytical side of both rather than the product roadmap. The work spans fraud victim reimbursement, chargeback resolution, operations time per complaint, AI adoption in operations, regulatory reporting, new security layers for customers, and a horizontal view of how fraud frictions affect customers' lives.

The Contestation Platform team is the analytical foundation for how Nubank handles customer reports and disputes, providing the best experience possible for customers who were fraud victims or had any issues with their credit card purchases. This includes an intuitive reporting flow, transparency in the process and fairness in reimbursements decisions. The focus for 2027 is how we can increase the AI usage in the platform to decrease total costs of our complaints, including decreasing losses and operational time spent to resolve a complaint.

The Security Features team is an innovative area, with the primary goal to make Nubank customers feel safer, and we do this by creating solutions that increase customers' perception of our defenses and also create new defenses. Our best example is Safe Mode (Modo Rua), an extra security layer that protects customers' investments and cash-out when we detect they are away from home/ safe wifi networks. The focus for 2027 is to understand why customers still believe Nubank is not the safest financial institution, even though we believe we have best-in-class fraud policies/models at least in BR, and after identifying the pain points, increase safety perception.

The Customer Analytics scope was once a dedicated pack and is now held by one of the Decision Intelligence analysts. It owns horizontal fraud views, trying to solve a historical gap we have in fraud, that teams are isolated in their silos, not having proper understanding of how different squads' defenses impact customers as a whole in their real life. The focus for 2027 is to ensure fraud squads understand their defenses' impact in customers' experience, and give CX the same weight as fraud losses for decision making.


You’ll be Responsible for

  • Lead the team: run weekly planning with the BAs, set priorities across the groups, guide day-to-day analytical work, and own hiring, feedback and career development for eight BAs, plus informal leadership of the two Analytics Engineers.

  • Partner with the three Contestation squads: work closely with the Squad Leads of Core, Conan and CCI to decide which problems to solve, how to measure them, and whether a rollouts or tests worked as expected or not

  • Own analytical quality: review critical analyses and recommendations before they reach leadership and decision forums, such as reimbursement policy changes and their financial impact.

  • Drive the AI agenda: lead the weekly forum where Product, Engineering, Operations and Analytics track the AI initiatives that automate complaint handling, and turn results into decisions.

  • Shape strategy and goals: build the yearly objectives and metrics with Product and Engineering leadership, and review the roadmap every month against what the data shows.

  • Represent analytics with partners: Operations in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, Finance on how losses are booked and reported, and Risk and Controls on audits and regulatory reports.

  • You will be accountable for the analytics of both scopes and for the people who deliver it. The team works with every country where Nubank operates, so English is part of the daily routine. In Contestation you are also the main driver of the AI reinvention of complaint handling

 

What We're Looking For Someone Who Has

  • Analytical capacity: ease with numbers and calculations, having the ability to solve problems mathematically;

  • Business basics: dynamics between risks and opportunities, as well as interaction between business areas and technical areas (products/engineering);

  • Problem solving: ease and creativity to seek solutions to day-to-day challenges and achieve the best results;

  • Ability to understand how your decisions and work impact our customers' experience, seeking results that align with our purpose;

  • Willingness and ease of learning, especially for tools;

  • A mix of fraud valuation and analytical-platform skills setting valuation methodology and governance, as well as building the AI-first tooling the rest of the BU runs on.

  • Openness to receive feedback and incorporate it into your daily life and development;

  • Adaptability to the multifunctional environment;

  • Profiles that add value to Nubank's culture.

  • English communication skills

 

Our Benefits

  • Chance of earning equity at Nubank

  • Food/ Meal Card (Vale-Refeição and/or Vale Alimentação)

  • Public Transportation Commuting Benefit (Vale-Transporte)

  • NuCare – Psychological, Financial and Legal Assistance Program

  • Life Insurance

  • Medical Plan

  • Dental Plan

  • NuLanguage – Language Course Program

  • Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

  • Extended Parental Leave

  • Daycare Allowance

  • Parental Consultancy

  • Work-from-home Allowance

  • Gym Partnerships

  • 30 days of paid vacation

  • Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable

Work Model for this Role

Hybrid 2-3 times/week: Our hybrid work model brings us to the office at least twice a week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit https://building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/

About Nu

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page

Marketing - Partnerships Activation Manager

This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.

About the role

Nu is looking for a Partnerships Activation Manager to bring our Sports & Entertainment Partnerships to life. You will own and drive core activations, turning partnership rights and opportunities into distinctive marketing, fan and customer experiences that support Nu’s business objectives.

Working closely with partners, agencies and teams across Nu, you will take work from brief to execution and evaluation. You’ll combine creative judgment with operational excellence: delivering the details consistently, bringing people together and finding opportunities to create moments that resonate beyond the event itself.

You’lll also help build the tools and ways of working that enable the team to deliver consistently and grow.

What you’ll do

  • Own day-to-day activation planning and delivery across assigned sports & entertainment partnerships, building strong relationships with partner teams and internal stakeholders.

  • Translate partnership and campaign objectives into clear activation plans, creative briefs, timelines, budgets and measures of success.

  • Track contractual rights and assets, coordinate approvals, and identify opportunities to use entitlements effectively. Flag delivery gaps early and support discussions on solutions or make-goods.

  • Brief and manage agencies and vendors delivering experiences, content, signage, hospitality and other partnership assets. Hold work to a high standard of creative quality, brand consistency and execution.

  • Plan and deliver event-day activations and partner moments, managing run-of-show, logistics, ticketing and accreditation where relevant and in line with Nu policies.

  • Bring Brand, Marketing, Creative, Communications, Legal, Compliance, Product and Analytics teams together to develop and deliver integrated work.

  • Manage budgets, forecasts, invoices and reconciliation for assigned activations, escalating risks early and recommending adjustments when needed.

  • Evaluate activations against agreed objectives, share clear learnings and recommend improvements that strengthen future work.

  • Build and improve practical playbooks, templates and partner-onboarding processes as the portfolio grows.

What we’re looking for

  • Relevant experience in partnership activation, sponsorship, brand or experiential marketing, or equivalent experience.

  • Demonstrated experience taking complex activations or campaigns from planning through execution and evaluation.

  • Understanding of sponsorship and how partnership rights and assets can create value for a brand and its audiences.

  • Experience managing agencies, vendors and cross-functional stakeholders, with the ability to build strong relationships and keep work moving across competing priorities.

  • Experience managing significant project budgets and timelines, with exceptional attention to detail and sound judgment when plans change.

  • Ability to develop clear briefs, assess creative work and turn performance information into practical recommendations.

  • Strong communication skills and confidence presenting plans, updates and recommendations to partners and senior stakeholders.

  • Willingness to travel and work some evenings and weekends around events.

Experience that would be a plus

  • Experience across sports or entertainment partnerships at a brand, agency, rights holder or property.

  • Experience building processes or playbooks in a growing organization.

  • An established network across the US sports and entertainment industry.

  • Multi-language

Location

  • Miami, United States

Our Benefits

  • Opportunity of earning equity at Nu

  • Medical Insurance

  • Dental and Vision Insurance

  • Life Insurance and AD&D

  • Extended maternity and paternity leaves

  • Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

  • NuLanguage - Our language learning program

  • NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program

  • 401K

  • Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account

  • Work-from-home Allowance

  • Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable.

Work Model for this Role

  • Hybrid 2-3 times/week: Our hybrid work model brings us to the office at least twice a week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit https://building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/
